title: Why two tides a day?
hook: There is one Moon and it pulls one way. So why does the sea rise twice a day?

knows: that tides rise and fall with the Moon
that the Earth spins once a day
doesNotKnow: why most coasts have two high tides a day
that there is a bulge on the side away from the Moon

misconception: The Moon pulls water into one bulge facing it, so there should be one high tide a day.
objective: The learner can explain that the Moon's pull differs across the Earth, stretching the ocean into two bulges, so a turning coast meets two highs per lunar day of about 24 h 50 min.

claims.text: On most ocean coasts there are two high tides in each lunar day, about 12 h 25 min apart.
claims.source: Principal lunar semidiurnal constituent M2, period 12.42 h; most of the world's coasts are semidiurnal or mixed (NOAA CO-OPS, 'Tides and Water Levels'; from memory, not checked online). 12 h 25 min = half of 24 h 50 min, computed in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: A lunar day, the time for a place to face the Moon again, is about 24 h 50 min.
claims.source: Mean lunar day 24 h 50 min 28 s (any almanac; NOAA; from memory). The Moon moves along its orbit in the same direction the Earth spins, so the Earth must turn a little more than once.

claims.text: The Moon pulls near-side water harder than the Earth's centre, and the centre harder than far-side water; the difference stretches the ocean into two bulges along the Moon line.
claims.source: Tidal acceleration is the difference of the Moon's gravity across the Earth, approximately 2 G M r / d^3 along the Earth-Moon line on both sides (Newtonian gravity). Equilibrium tide height goes as cos(2 x angle from the Moon) plus a constant, which is what the stage draws (with a made-up amplitude).

claims.text: Real coasts differ, and some get only one tide a day.
claims.source: Diurnal tides occur on some coasts, e.g. parts of the Gulf of Mexico and Southeast Asia (NOAA tide classifications; from memory, not checked online). The stage labels itself 'Toy: no continents, bulges exaggerated'.

recall.question: High tide at a beach is at 8:00 in the morning. Roughly when is the next high tide?
recall.why: There are two bulges, one toward the Moon and one away, so a coast meets a high every half lunar day, about 12 h 25 min.
